sources.title: Gastrointestinal parasites of endemic and endangered free-ranging purple-faced leaf monkey (Semnopithecus vetulus) in Sri Lanka: effect of host group size and habitat type
sources.locator: Abstract; study period, fecal sampling, parasite prevalence, host group-size and habitat comparisons.

sources.licenseAppliesTo: The publisher preview exposes the abstract and identifies the full article as subscription content. This guide paraphrases the abstract-level findings only.
sources.attribution: Weerasekara L, Wijesooriya K, Ranawana K, Anupama T, Rajapakse J. 2021. Gastrointestinal parasites of endemic and endangered free-ranging purple-faced leaf monkey (Semnopithecus vetulus) in Sri Lanka: effect of host group size and habitat type. Primates 62:629–635. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10329-021-00902-0.
sources.scope: Fresh fecal samples collected from free-ranging Semnopithecus vetulus in Sri Lanka between December 2017 and April 2019; findings describe sampled groups and habitats, not the complete species range.

claims.text: The study analyzed 78 fresh fecal samples collected in Sri Lanka from December 2017 through April 2019; 55% contained at least one gastrointestinal parasite type.
claims.scope: Sample-level detection in the surveyed free-ranging groups; not a clinical disease estimate for all purple-faced leaf monkeys.

claims.text: Trichuris trichiura was the most prevalent helminth reported (15%). Its prevalence was significantly related to troop size; the study also reported habitat differences for T. trichiura and Ascaris lumbricoides.
claims.scope: Associations reported in the sampled groups; the design does not establish causal effects or species-wide patterns.

claims.text: Fecal parasite findings do not demonstrate transmission between monkeys and people or diagnose clinical illness in an individual monkey.
claims.scope: Interpretive boundary; human infection and individual clinical outcomes were not established by the reported fecal survey.

gaps: This is a local research guide, not a general account of purple-faced leaf monkey morphology, distribution, diet, or life history.
The surveyed groups do not establish current range-wide parasite prevalence or causal effects of troop size and habitat.
The publisher preview did not confirm an open license; this record supports attribution and paraphrase only.
